subtitle: 'A Marvellous Work and a Wonder': Isaiah 13–14; 22; 24–30; 35

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.summary: Sweeping prophetic arc from Babylon's fall to the Restoration — trace judgment → mercy → warning → restoration.
sections.body: This week's readings present a complete prophetic arc.
bullets: Babylon's fall = type for pride of the world
Key of David = Christ's authority over life/death
Spiritual danger comes from within, not without

sections.heading: Key Doctrine
sections.summary: Core messianic prophecies and their fulfillment.
sections.body: Isaiah contains five key messianic prophecies.

rows: Christ holds authority over life, death, and salvation

sections.heading: Application Questions
bullets: Q: How do I recognize pride in my life? | A: The pattern is self-exaltation above God's will | S: Isaiah 14:13–14; Moses 4:1–4 | W: Recognizing the pattern helps us identify it in our own hearts

Q: When I feel spiritually drunk, how do I sober up? | A: Return to the Source of truth through scripture and prayer | S: Isaiah 1:18; 35:8 | W: Daily scripture study + prayer = spiritual sobriety test
